gen-bebas-neue-fs-paquito: Bebas Neue packs its letters into a tight, uniform band of capitals, trimmed-looking and close, with no stroke contrast whatsoever. Paquito, confident and approachable, stays pleasant in modest helpings.
gen-boska-fs-asap: Chiseled drama: Boska's stems feel carved from stone, its serifs scratched into glass. Asap takes the other job: open arcs on its c and a body height close to the capitals.
gen-boska-fs-familjen-grotesk: Dramatic and bookish, Boska has hairline crossbars on stems thick as fence posts. Familjen Grotesk runs lively and tall in the lowercase, so paragraphs keep moving without tiring the eye.
gen-boska-fs-public-sans: Public Sans brings a hefty lowercase and broad open counters, set beneath Boska's hairline curves running into bold stems. Long stretches of it feel steady, trustworthy and pleasantly unhurried.
gen-boska-fs-roundo: Fat strokes beside fine ones, then tidy geometry. Boska earns its keep big and short, while Roundo's sans keeps an n with arch and stem matching and every small counter unclogged.
gen-boska-fs-synonym: Bold stress, hairline counterstrokes, then a plain stripe of constant ink. Boska earns its keep big and short, while Synonym's dependable sans leaves generous openings in every single curve.
gen-boska-gf-lexend-tera: Dramatic swells up top, then a plotter-pen line below. Boska's pronounced thick-and-thin rhythm meets Lexend Tera's stepping-stone spacing, so dense ink and generous room trade places down the page.
gen-boska-mulish: Razor-thin hairlines on Boska's fat stems, then one steady stylus. Mulish traces each stroke at stylus width, with horseshoe-open apertures and a large x-height, so long reading feels modern and friendly.
gen-boska-outfit: Boska's dazzling push and pull of fat and fine sets the tone. Outfit stays out of the way, its cable-like curves finishing well before they close, so longer reading feels clean and approachable.
gen-boska-poppins: Dramatic and bookish, Boska stands at moderate lowercase height with carved-stone stems. And Poppins, taller in the lowercase with rope-loose curves, gives that drama a steady, modern place to land.
